body: Character look: chunky, rounded, bean-shaped toy-like party-game characters. Big heads joined to round pill-shaped bodies, short stubby arms and legs, glossy vinyl-toy surfaces, goofy expressive faces with big eyes, bright saturated colors. Each one wears a fun costume skin. Original characters only, not any known game character, mascot, or brand.
world: The place is a giant redwood forest at golden hour, with huge red tree trunks, ferns, and light rays through the mist. American setting, not East Asian.
battle: A screenshot of a 2D side-view video game battle between two chunky toy characters. Both are mid-attack and face each other, one on the left and one on the right. On the left, a character in a park-ranger costume with a ranger hat and a badge vest fires a glowing slingshot. On the right, a character in a fuzzy bigfoot costume swings a glowing hockey stick. Simple game UI: two health bars at the top, one for each fighter, each with a small portrait of its fighter. At the bottom, a panel with the math question "7 × 8 = ?" and 4 answer buttons: 54, 56, 63, 48. All 4 buttons look the same; no button is lit or picked. Cool, exciting, and fun for a 10-year-old. Weapon effects are bright energy sparks and streaks, not fire, water, rock, or wind magic. No text other than the UI. No logos, no brands.
lineup: A character select screen of a video game: 6 chunky toy characters stand in a row, side by side, all facing the viewer and doing happy poses. From left to right: 1 a park ranger with a ranger hat and a badge vest, 2 a lumberjack in a red flannel shirt with an axe, 3 a fuzzy brown bigfoot costume, 4 a white astronaut suit with a helmet, 5 a hot dog costume with mustard, 6 a cowboy with a hat and boots. Fun for a 10-year-old. No text, no UI, no logos, no brands.

variants.name: 3D toys in a painted forest
variants.style: Art style: the characters are smooth 3D-rendered toys with soft plastic shading. They stand in an HD-2D scene: a painterly world with soft 3D-looking depth, warm volumetric light, glow, bloom, and depth-of-field blur in the foreground and background.
variants.note: The characters need 3D models. We can also render the 3D models into sprite sheets for the 2D engine.

variants.name: Chunky pixel toys
variants.style: Art style: HD-2D. The characters are crisp pixel-art sprites with the chunky toy shape. They are placed in a scene with soft 3D-looking depth, warm volumetric light, glow, bloom, and depth-of-field blur in the foreground and background.
variants.note: This style works with the 2D engine as it is. Pixel sprites are fast to draw and animate.

variants.name: Full 3D toy world
variants.style: Art style: full stylized 3D. Both the characters and the world are bright, smooth, toy-like 3D renders with clean shapes, soft shadows, and cheerful color, like a party video game.
variants.note: The characters and the world need 3D models. This is the most work, but it gives the most polish.
